title: HTTP3: remove nghttp3 version requirement, update setup scripts, update Homebrew
description:
* CI,Tools: auto-enable Homebrew updates in CI, remove brew doctor

    * Show brew and homebrew-core versions to learn about available formula.
    * The formula list included with the current macOS image is too old and
      does not have libnghttp3. Enable auto-updates to resolve this, these
      are faster than before: https://brew.sh/2023/02/16/homebrew-4.0.0/
    * Disable brew doctor, it breaks CI for non-fatal reasons.

* HTTP3: remove nghttp3 min version, update setup scripts

    * The QPACK decoder code has not significantly changed since the initial
      nghttp3 0.1.0 release. The `user_data` field of `nghttp3_mem` was
      renamed from `mem_user_data` in 0.2.0. Since we do not use it, just
      remove the field to make it build on Ubuntu 22.04 with 0.1.1.
    * Arch Linux, BSD, Debian, Alpine: add (lib)nghttp3.
    * debian/control: add libnghttp3-dev dependency.
    * brew: Install libnghttp2 instead of nghttp2, we only need the library.
    * brew: libnghttp3 was just made available in Homebrew, so install it:
      https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/150922

___
After merging this, we have to rebuild the Ubuntu (22.04) and debian-stable images in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/

Otherwise the next Ubuntu and Debian APT package build will fail. This build is ran twice a day 7:00 and 19:00 UTC). I'll make sure that the containers are rebuilt between these intervals.

I plan to backport this to the release-4.2 branch.

notes.body: requested review from @geraldcombs, @johnthacker, and @alagoutte

The macOS build keeps failing, I already retried two times. No idea how often the Homebrew Formulae are being updated in the macOS VM. If this is still a problem tomorrow, I am considering adding a `brew update` to `.gitlab-ci.yaml`.

```
$ ./tools/macos-setup-brew.sh --install-optional --install-test-deps
Warning: Treating cmake as a formula. For the cask, use homebrew/cask/cmake
Warning: No available formula with the name "libnghttp3". Did you mean libnghttp2 or lighttpd?
==> Searching for similarly named formulae and casks...
==> Formulae
libnghttp2
lighttpd
To install libnghttp2, run:
  brew install libnghttp2
```

According to [update policy documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/runners/saas/macos_saas_runner.html#image-update-policy-for-macos) we might be able to pick up an updated Homebrew by switching from the `macos-12-xcode-14` image to the `macos-12-xcode-14:latest` image. If that doesn't work I'm OK with adding `brew update`, although it will likely increase our build times.

Can you add `brew --version` to the job as well? That should give us a better clue about where we stand.

Thanks for the pointer, the reason why I keep getting older versions makes a lot of sense now.

The VM uses an image that has brew pre-installed. Based on your linked docs, it is not entirely clear what the current "stable image" version refers to. I hope it is newer than February 2023, that should include Homebrew 4.0.0 which has a much faster "update" operation where it uses an external API instead of updating the large homebrew-core repository.

The Ansible playbooks linked in the GitLab documentation has commands to tap (clone) the homebrew-core repo. This made sense before 4.0.0 as it was a standard, slow operation. It also has `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1` enabled to disable fetching newer versions of packages.

Due to `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, all formula would be stuck in the past. Waiting a day, or even weeks would probably not help.

In the most recent push, I have set the following in an attempt to get newer formula, hopefully from the API instead of the homebrew-core tap:
```shell
HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API="" HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE="" brew install libnghttp3
```
but based on empirical testing, I am afraid that all local taps might be updated. I've added some timing to see if this is bearable.

I hope that this works, upgrading the full macOS image might have other side effects such as bringing in new compiler versions. Not necessary a bad thing, but it changes more variables.

Okay this is very old, it would never have been able to install the libnghttp3 package for up to months:
```
$ brew --version
Homebrew 4.0.14
Homebrew/homebrew-core (git revision 3cd1cf147d5; last commit 2023-04-18)
```

The explicit command added in this MR took 23 seconds.
Installing pre-requisites through brew took 5:26 in a [recent job](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/5295837249), and only 3:09 in this PR. Not sure why it is even faster, but it suggests that the workaround is acceptable?

Note that as side-effect, we get new versions for verything. In the older job, Qt 6.4.3 with OpenSSL 1.1.1t were installed whereas this MR causes Qt 6.5.2 with OpenSSL 3.1.3 to be installed.

@geraldcombs Do you want to go ahead and merge this or would you like to think more about it?
there is not some issue with Qt 6.5.x and MacOS ?

There may be issues, but I am not aware of them. I have been using Wireshark built from Git on an Intel MBP for a while with no problems. Note that these CI builds will only be used for testing commits, there is no artifact downloadable by users.

I just pushed a new version where I removed the manual `brew install libnghttp3` in favor of removing `HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE`.

https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ci-cd/shared-runners/images/job-images/-/blob/main/toolchain/macos-13.yml#L7
https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ci-cd/shared-runners/images/job-images/-/blob/56839a65fea253bd5808956d5d22bdeacfab266e/ansible/playbooks/homebrew.yml#L91-97

I have also removed the explicit `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API` variable, it was only set for the `brew update` command used during the GitLab VM image build.

If this is again an improvement over the `setup-macos-brew.sh` times we had before, maybe it is good to go with the proposed auto-updating behavior.

I've opened https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ci-cd/shared-runners/macos/-/issues/37 with some of the issues that I found here.

I realize we are close to the 4.2.0rc2 deadline, so would like to get this in the sooner than later to expand testing coverage.

> I realize we are close to the 4.2.0rc2 deadline, so would like to get this in the sooner than later to expand testing coverage.

Sounds good. I'm generally more concerned about minimizing build times than having the latest software in our MR jobs, but we don't have much choice in this case. I'll go ahead and merge this.

Adding nghttp3 here made it a mandatory lib for debian builds, while it's still an optional lib general everywhere else. Even the debian-setup.sh keeps it as optional. Remove?

The `debian-setup.sh` script marks both libnghttp2-dev and libnghttp3-dev as optional.

The `libnghttp3-dev` library is available since Debian Bookworm (current stable) and Ubuntu 22.04. If you are running older versions, you can consider patching this file to remove the `libnghttp3-dev` build dependency. Would that be sufficient for your purposes?

What distribution and version are you targetting?
I'm still building for some Ubuntu 20.04 users, where libnghttp3 is non-exist :/ If MR to remove this line is fine I will make one.

No, I don't think it is acceptable to remove this package in `packaging/debian/control` file as that would affect all other users of more modern systems.

Since you have to copy from `packaging/debian/` to `debian/`, can you add an extra command to remove the dependency just for the Ubuntu build?

E.g.
```sh
sed -e 's/ libnghttp3-dev,//' -i debian/control
```
or
```sh
sed -e 's/ libnghttp3-dev,//' packaging/debian/control > debian/control
```
For sure, not doing that many builds for this OS so there is no problem just removing line temporarily for now until the users has moved on to newer Ubuntu

commits_data.message:
CI,Tools: auto-enable Homebrew updates in CI, remove brew doctor

* Show brew and homebrew-core versions to learn about available formula.

  does not have libnghttp3. Enable auto-updates to resolve this, these
  are faster than before: https://brew.sh/2023/02/16/homebrew-4.0.0/
* Disable brew doctor, it breaks CI for non-fatal reasons.
